newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHARES EXTEND SLIGHT GAINS, MORE SEEN.
newsitem.headline: SHARES EXTEND SLIGHT GAINS, MORE SEEN.

text.p: * Official list index inches up 5.96 points to 960.86, group A up 1.79 points to 1,860.17.
* Central market volume 620,000 litas. Bloc trades turn over 660,000 litas. Secondary T-bill market turns over almost ten million litas.
* Hermis Bank gains to 221 litas from 216 litas. Vilnoaus Bank up slightly to 245.20 litas from 245 litas.
Lithuanian shares extended their recent slight gains on Tuesday and dealers said that more were on the horizon as investors are lured by bargain prices.
The official list index rose 5.96 points to 960.86 while the wider group A index crept up 1.79 points to 1,860.17.

Central market volume was 620,000 litas while block trades generated 660,000 litas worth of volume. The secondary T-bill market was relatively active with almost ten million litas worth of paper swapping hands.
Hermis Bank led the official list gainers as it added five litas to 221 litas in trade of almost 160,000 litas.
The bank, which was once widely viewed as undervalued, has risen from around 185 litas in the past few weeks and some dealers feel it is now in its proper price range and won't go much further.
Rival Vilniaus Bank, which announced its audited interim results on Tuesday after the price fix, inched up to 245.20 litas from 245 litas.
Dealers said it could rise further as the market digests its results, which showed a net profit of 21.7 million litas compared to 11.7 million litas for the same period last year.
Brokers said that further gains were seen for most major shares over the next weeks as buyers are tempted back to the market by low prices.
The market has struggled recently through a bout of summer-induced sluggishness.
